review_notes: The cleaned clip shows a droplet impacting the liquid-infused surface, deforming into a necked contact shape, retracting under surface tension, and bouncing back upward. A single frame could show only a droplet or an intermediate deformation; the named concept requires the full impact-retraction-liftoff sequence. Source text double-checks the droplet-impact/bouncing context, while the video itself supplies the temporal evidence. Overlay text, audio, and metadata were removed.

The cleaned microscopy time-lapse shows a GFP-tagged pollen tube extending and navigating into the ovule structure over time. A single frame shows only a tube-like fluorescence trace; the VDCR answer depends on observing directional tip growth and navigation. The source page double-checks short-range ovule-signal attraction/repulsion, while the video provides the directed growth trajectory. Time labels, scale bars, audio, and metadata were removed.

The cleaned microscopy time-lapse shows an elongating root hair with the growing tip advancing across frames. A static image can identify a root-hair-like structure, but cannot establish polarized tip growth; the concept requires temporal extension of the tip. The source page double-checks root-hair polarity/elongation, while the video itself shows the extension sequence. Timestamp overlays, audio, and metadata were removed.

The source is a long explanatory animation with frequency readouts, wave symbols, formula-like labels, and audio.
